title: Microscopy and Microanalysis Methods for Diagnosing Plastic Part Molding Defects – Real-World Case Studies
content: The manufacture of plastic parts through injection molding requires tight control of the viscoelastic and crystallization properties of the molten polymer as it flows through complex molds with large temperature gradients and shear rate [1]. Loss of control of those properties can result in both structural and visual defects in the parts, which may result in excess scrap material and the loss of production time [2]. Microscopy techniques such as polarized light microscopy (PLM) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) can provide unique contributions to investigations into the cause of many part defects, allowing for faster, more evidence-based resolution to manufacturing process questions [3].
